SHAREGAIN.quote: improving by about 1100bps from about 11% -- from about 8% to about 18.6% in Q4 FY '26

CULTURE.rationale: Within this 12-month window management repeatedly made specific promises and delivered them — the 700-store target guided in Q2 was hit by March '26, and the Middle India focus called out in Q1 produced the promised share — and bad news was disclosed and quantified promptly (rare-earth supply crunch, unfiled subsidies, INR20-25 crore EBITDA hit). Judgement is limited to one year of listed history, with no return-on-capital framing and a still loss-making P&L.
CULTURE.quote: There was roughly, I would think, about a INR20 crores subsidy that we haven't filed for in Q2. We expect this to be a one-time hit

MOATTEST.rationale: There are real replication costs — a 643-patent portfolio, an in-house software stack with measured daily usage, 700 stores plus service and charging networks built over a decade — but the calls also show well-capitalised incumbents contesting the same markets and acknowledge 'very strong competitive intensity', and nothing described is un-replicable by a funded rival over a few years.
MOATTEST.quote: about 50,000 power users who use navigation every single day now

RECURRING.rationale: Across all four FY26–Q1FY27 calls there is no discussion of AMC/service contracts, spares, renewals, attach rates or customer advances as a funding source; revenue is recognised on dispatch/FAT/site-acceptance milestones only.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales go directly to utilities and developers through competitive tenders (GETCO, RVPNL, PSTCL, Adani Green, BNC Power Projects), with management noting 'most customer tenders are floated during the initial part of the financial year' — the buyer is the payer, and there is no prescriber/installer channel or trade-training programme anywhere in the calls.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: most customer tenders are floated during the initial part of the financial year

TOLLROAD.rationale: The certification/qualification anchoring is genuinely toll-road-like — PGCIL approval, seven NABL-accredited test labs, and management's point that 'the approval qualification process of the power sector tender takes 12 to 18 months' — but the core economic test fails: a 160–315 MVA power transformer is a large capital line item for the customer, not a <1-2% consumable, and pricing is set by tender rather than accepted without negotiation.
TOLLROAD.quote: the approval qualification process of the power sector tender takes 12 to 18 months

LOWPRICE.rationale: The stated strategy is the opposite of low-price-plus: deliberate mix shift up the voltage curve into segments 'where entry barriers and margins are structurally higher', with 220 kV now ~52% of FY26 revenue and EBITDA margin expanding 300bps to 18.6%. LOWPRICE.quote: Expand into higher kV class MVA classes, where entry barriers and margins are structurally higher

PRICING.rationale: Management explicitly attributes Q1 FY27's 48% growth to volume with no price effect, and on rising input costs describes passing on only 'a significant portion' — cost pass-through under contract terms, not price increases above cost inflation. Margin gains are credited to operating leverage and mix, never to pricing.
PRICING.quote: there were no material changes in pricing or product mix, with the growth largely attributable to increased production capacity

BRAND.rationale: What exists is B2B reputational capital rather than brand equity — 'three decades of customer relationship', 4,700 transformers/1,07,000 MVA supplied across 19 states, 251 clients, and repeat orders from GETCO described as reflecting long partnership. But there is no A&P spend, no premium pricing, and no adjacency stretch under the name.
BRAND.quote: These orders reflect deep trust built over three decades of partnership with Gujarat's premier state transmission utility.

INNOVATION.rationale: No R&D spend, pipeline, or named-product revenue contribution is disclosed in any of the four calls; capability expansion (400/765 kV class, inverter duty transformers, ester-oil green transformers) is presented as capex and qualification milestones rather than as an innovation engine, so the evidence is silent on this pattern.

FORWARD.rationale: There is no own-store, franchise, licensing or D2C motion — the company sells direct to utilities via tender, and its integration move is in the opposite direction, toward inputs: 'the tank and radiator backward integration initiatives'.
FORWARD.quote: including the new inverter duty transformer facility and the tank and radiator backward integration initiatives

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Growth is far above any plausible industry rate — FY26 revenue +48.8% to INR1,851.5cr, Q3 +80% YoY, order book to a record INR3,116cr on record Q1 FY27 inflow of INR972cr — and capacity went 16,000 to 63,000 MVA, but management never cites a market-share number or a share position against named competitors, so persistent share gain is inferred, not evidenced.
SHAREGAIN.quote: The company recorded its highest-ever quarterly order inflow of INR972.42 crores.

CULTURE.rationale: Within the window, promises made on calls were delivered on later calls: the Q3 FY26 debt-reduction commitment was fully honoured (INR340cr term loans to nil by 31 March 2026, ahead of schedule), FY26 growth of 48.8% beat the 40% target set for the year, and capex is now funded from accruals. CULTURE.quote: I'm pleased to confirm that we have delivered fully on the debt reduction commitment made during Q3 FY '26.

MOATTEST.rationale: Real barriers exist — PGCIL/NABL approvals, short-circuit test capability, seven accredited labs, 12–18 month qualification cycles and a three-decade reference list — but management's own 'Atlanta speed' claim of groundbreaking to PGCIL 400 kV approval in two years shows a well-funded entrant can build the same position in a few years, which is exactly what the cost-to-replicate test screens out.
MOATTEST.quote: This was achieved within just two years of groundbreaking at Vadod

RECURRING.rationale: Banking relationships are inherently recurring and management describes monetising the installed base — cross-sell department, 15+ bancassurance partners, wealth AUM, SA accounts opened to existing asset customers — but no attach rates, renewal rates or deferred-revenue funding discipline is quantified in the way the pattern requires.
RECURRING.quote: we saw promising results with 95,000 SA accounts opened in the last 6 months... Our insurance penetration is increasing, and we have now added LIC and SBI Life as our bancassurance partners

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Parts of the asset book are originated through professional intermediaries — vehicle dealers/partners for Wheels, partner-led distribution, and an ICAI-linked chartered-accountant banking programme — but lending is price-negotiated by the end borrower, so the low price-sensitivity core of the pattern is absent.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: Vehicle partners' onboarding for Wheels loans is live and additional integrations that deepen STP journeys and partner-led distribution are underway

TOLLROAD.rationale: Credit and deposits are the customer's main cost, not a trivial line item, and the calls repeatedly describe an intensely competitive, rate-driven market rather than a rational oligopoly customers cannot leave.
TOLLROAD.quote: The deposit environment, however, remains intensely competitive with tight liquidity conditions

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is genuine cost discipline — cost-to-assets down 19bps to 4.1% in FY26, businesses merged, parallel hierarchies eliminated, agentic AI used to grow without proportional headcount — but AU is a high-yield lender that competes on service and reach, not a low-price operator passing savings to customers.
LOWPRICE.quote: realigning our organizational structure by consolidating businesses, eliminating parallel hierarchies, and reducing redundancy... without proportional increase in cost or headcount

PRICING.rationale: The liability-side evidence is real: 75bps of SA rate cuts through FY26 while deposits still grew 23-24% YoY at ~1.8x system, with NIM rising 5.4%→5.5%→5.7%→5.96%. But this rides a falling-rate cycle and CRR benefit rather than demonstrated price rises above cost inflation.
PRICING.quote: we have cut peak SA rate by another 25 bps, taking the total SA rate cut in highest bucket to 75 bps in this financial year

BRAND.rationale: Sustained brand investment (Ranbir Kapoor/Rashmika Mandanna ambassadors, 'Soch Badlo aur Bank Bhi' campaign) and a 30-year franchise heritage, with management explicitly expecting the universal licence to lift brand acceptance — but the brand is not yet shown to command premium pricing; AU still pays above-system deposit rates.
BRAND.quote: Universal banking license will significantly enhance trust and brand acceptance among depositors, enabling the bank to optimize its cost of funds over time

INNOVATION.rationale: Consistent, disclosed investment (8-10% of OPEX in technology for 8 years) with named launches each quarter — AI-native gold loan LOS live, agentic AI platform extending to mortgages/wheels/cards, Customer 360, M Circle, multicurrency forex card — though this is operational digitisation funding efficiency, not high-gross-margin R&D driving industry dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: Over the past 8 years, we have consistently and strategically invested 8%-10% of our OPEX in our technology backbone

FORWARD.rationale: AU owns its distribution end-to-end — 2,726 physical touchpoints with ~100 branches added per year and >90% of transactions running through its own AU 0101 platform — but for a bank direct distribution is the baseline model, not a deliberate move down the value chain.
FORWARD.quote: more than 90% of the bank's transactions and service requests now being processed through AU 0101

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Every one of the four calls quantifies growth as a multiple of system: deposits 21%→23%→23%→24% YoY (1.8-2x system), loans 17%→19.3%→21%→23% (1.3-1.7x), Q1FY27 disbursements +42%. Critically, share was not bought with credit quality — GNPA fell 2.30%→2.03% and credit cost fell from 1.4% to 0.8% over the same window.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Deposits growth remained robust at 24% year-on-year, significantly ahead of the estimated private sector banking deposit growth of 14%. Loan portfolio grew by 23% year-on-year versus private sector banking growth of 17%

CULTURE.rationale: Founder-led for 30 years with Sanjay Agarwal's tenure extended to 2029, deliberate succession depth (Vivek Tripathi to ED, Yogesh Jain to Deputy CEO, three new independent directors, new CRO), open acknowledgement of the unsecured/MFI stress cycle quarter by quarter rather than burying it, and an explicit admission of error — plus long-horizon capex into distribution, brand and technology.
CULTURE.quote: We have learned from our mistakes and acted quickly, positioning AU to deliver a sustainable and predictable growth beyond 2027

MOATTEST.rationale: There are articulable barriers a funded newcomer cannot shortcut — an RBI universal banking licence granted after a 30-year track record, a pan-India branch and liability franchise built over 8.5 years, and an acquired bank giving South India presence — but management itself concedes deposits remain intensely contested on price, which is the part of the moat a rival can attack with capital.
MOATTEST.quote: we received an in-principle approval from the Reserve Bank of India to become a universal bank... This is a strong endorsement of AU's business model, sound governance

RECURRING.rationale: Across all four FY26 calls the revenue conversation is order-book and project-execution driven (Rs.1,800 crore order book, go-lives, milestone completions) with no disclosure of AMC/licence share, attach rates or renewals; the working-capital signature is the opposite of customer-funded — DSOs of 100-110, negative H1 operating cash flow of ~Rs.80-86 crore, and management guiding to higher upfront working capital in FY27.
RECURRING.quote: larger projects bringing higher working capital needs as they scale

BRAND.rationale: The calls show reputational pull in enterprise banking — 'platform and partner of choice', 'go-to single-window data center provider', a refreshed brand identity in Q1 FY26 and marquee public-sector references — but there is no heritage story, no A&P spend, and no evidence of premium pricing attached to the name.
BRAND.quote: It reinforces our position as the platform as well as the partner of choice for large financial institutions.

INNOVATION.rationale: R&D is disclosed and guided at 9-10% of revenue every quarter, with named product output each period (Fenixys/Fintra additions, AurionAi, Orion-MSP and TabTune from Lexsi Labs, an agentic AI-native trade finance platform) and AI labs in Mumbai, Paris and London; management ties Rs.1,000 crore of cumulative product/acquisition spend since the FY22 pivot directly to the growth record.
INNOVATION.quote: Since that pivot four years back, we have invested more than Rs. 1,000 crore in new product development and in strategic acquisitions.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Record logo additions are reported every quarter of the window (16 in Q1, 19 in Q2 for a record 35 in H1, 23 in Q3) alongside named displacement wins (UCO Bank, a Singapore-headquartered bank for Integro, Delhi Metro AFC, a hyperscaler data centre mandate) and 20-29% growth while, as one analyst noted on the Q4 call, the wider Indian IT sector struggles — though management never quotes an explicit market-share percentage.
SHAREGAIN.quote: We added 23 new logos across our business segments, one of the fastest rates of customer additions in our journey so far.

CULTURE.rationale: The Q4 FY26 call is unusually candid about a miss — management named the 20.2% outcome against a ~30% plan, took the Q4 shortfall as its own responsibility rather than blaming only the MEA war, and admitted five years of fast growth had 'left us stretched in places'; leadership is stable (Zaveri and Sheth as promoters through FY21-FY26, Vipul Parmar as CFO throughout) and capital is being pushed into organic R&D rather than payouts.
CULTURE.quote: By our own standards, the final result was below par. We can do better and we will.

MOATTEST.rationale: There are real replication barriers — Rs.1,000 crore of accumulated product build, entrenched core transaction-banking and lending installs at public sector banks, safety-critical metro AFC/PSD credentials and proprietary banking foundation models — but management itself says the classic enterprise software mode is being disrupted by AI and that recent shocks 'exposed those vulnerabilities', so the barrier is not shown to be un-crossable by a well-funded AI-native entrant.
MOATTEST.quote: Owning the full stack is what separates an average vendor from a category leader

RECURRING.rationale: The four FY26 calls discuss product sales, tenders and launches only — no licence fees, AMC/service contracts, attach rates, renewals or customer advances are mentioned anywhere.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Nothing in the FY26 calls describes prescribers, installers or trade professionals driving demand; revenue is discussed through geographies, tenders and distributor/customer supply, with no channel-training or professional-relationship investment disclosed.

TOLLROAD.rationale: The API/KSM business behaves like a price-taking commodity, not a toll road: API revenue fell 16% YoY in Q1 FY26 on pricing pressure, and the Pen-G ramp depends on the government imposing a minimum import price rather than on customers paying without negotiating.
TOLLROAD.quote: we have made our representation to the government to implement the minimum import price, which will support the further ramp-up

LOWPRICE.rationale: Scale and cost competitiveness are the explicit strategy — capacity above 60 billion units, backward integration into Pen-G/6APA/Amoxicillin, a low-cost China OSD site — but the calls give no itemised cost-culture detail, and margins are held at a target 20-21% EBITDA rather than being reinvested into price.
LOWPRICE.quote: Our strategy on PEN-G and 6APA and Amoxicillin represents a structurally important initiative that will enhance cost competitiveness, reduce external dependencies and strengthen margin

PRICING.rationale: Across all four FY26 calls pricing is at best 'stable' and frequently a headwind: API revenue declined on pricing pressure (Q1), and the specialty/injectable business grew only after being 'partly offset by pricing pressures' (Q4). Price stability is credited to portfolio breadth, not pricing power.
PRICING.quote: Our large product portfolio helps us to maintain optimally the price stability

BRAND.rationale: The FY26 calls make no heritage, A&P, premium-pricing or brand-stretch claims; performance is attributed to volumes, launches, supply reliability and geography mix. There is not enough evidence either way on brand within this window.

INNOVATION.rationale: R&D is disclosed and rising in absolute terms (₹367cr Q1 → ₹414cr Q2 → ₹409cr Q3; ₹1,590cr FY26, ~5% of sales) with a steady cadence of launches (15, 6, 9 products) plus biosimilars, peptides and biologics CMO — but this is generic/complex-generic development funding volume, not high-margin innovation producing pricing power.
INNOVATION.quote: R&D expenditure stood at ■1,590 crores, which is 5% of revenue

FORWARD.rationale: No own-store, franchise, licensing or D2C economics are discussed in the FY26 calls; the integration described is backward into APIs/KSMs, and US/India expansion is via acquisitions (Lannett, Khandelwal, Acrotech) rather than direct-to-customer channels.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Europe shows persistent, accelerating gains through FY26 (9% → 18% → 27% YoY, crossing the promised €1bn), ARV grew 33% for the year on tender wins, and Canada/India were added — but management never cites share percentages or names competitors, and US revenue actually fell 18% YoY in Q4 on constant currency.
SHAREGAIN.quote: For the full year, European formulations achieved a significant milestone of €1 billion revenue

Management also volunteered a list of capex where revenue had slipped, though delays (Raleigh, China breakeven pushed Q3 → Q3-Q4 → Q4) are stated flatly rather than examined.
CULTURE.quote: the following areas where CapEx has been done and where revenues have been delayed include the following

MOATTEST.rationale: Some genuinely slow-to-replicate assets are evident — 60bn+ units of regulator-approved capacity, multi-year ANDA/EU filing stocks, and the only large integrated Pen-G fermentation chain in India — but the Pen-G economics rest on a one-year government minimum import price, and the core oral-solid generic business is replicable by any funded competitor.
MOATTEST.quote: The Government of India issued a notification introducing a one-year CIF on minimum import price for Pen-G, 6 APA and Amoxicillin

RECURRING.rationale: Management repeatedly calls existing-business revenue 'recurring', but this is repeat build orders from long product life cycles, not license/AMC/subscription streams — there are no attach rates, renewal rates or installed-base metrics, and working capital is firmly positive (112 days in Mar 2026, down from 124), so customers are not funding the business via advances.
RECURRING.quote: long product life cycles, mission-critical programs and recurring revenues

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The calls describe direct OEM contract manufacturing relationships with no professional/installer/prescriber channel, training programmes for a trade, or end-customer-vs-specifier split; the evidence is simply silent on this pattern.

TOLLROAD.rationale: There is genuine qualification-based lock-in — first article inspection in aerospace, Kavach testing and approval, semiconductor 'project readiness phase' — and mission-critical box builds that management says drive stickiness; but an EMS assembly is a large share of the customer's product cost, not the <1-2% toll, and there is no certification/gold-standard or oligopoly language.
TOLLROAD.quote: Our mantra to focus on mission-critical complex box builds continue to gain traction.

LOWPRICE.rationale: The India base is positioned explicitly as the low-cost, scalable option and the model is capex-light with very high asset turns (7.5x FY25 to ~9.9x FY26) and ROCE up to 20.6% — the high-turns/strong-returns signature; but there is no itemised cost-saving culture and management claims 'industry-leading' 34% gross margins rather than passing savings to price.
LOWPRICE.quote: We continue to follow a capex-light model. Asset turns are approximately 9.9 times.

PRICING.rationale: Avalon demonstrably passes through cost shocks — over 50 distinct tariff rates with 99%+ recovery from customers over two years of calls — and gross margin held at the top of the 33-35% band, but this is cost pass-through in a guided band, not price increases above inflation; Q4 FY26 gross margin actually eased to 33.7% as volumes scaled.
PRICING.quote: we were able to recover 99% of the applicable tariffs from our customers

BRAND.rationale: No heritage story, A&P spend, distributor leverage or consumer-facing brand is discussed anywhere in the four calls; this is a B2B contract manufacturer and the evidence is silent.

INNOVATION.rationale: Named new programs arrive every quarter with stated revenue timing — semiconductor equipment box builds, Kavach, satellite antenna control units, energy storage, locomotive engine subsystems — and complexity is rising (box build 44% four years ago to 56% in Q4 FY26); but no R&D spend is disclosed or discussed, and the IP is the customer's, so this is engineering capability rather than R&D-funded innovation dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: In semiconductor equipment, we have completed the project readiness phase with our global partner

FORWARD.rationale: No own stores, franchising, licensing or D2C activity is mentioned; the dual-shore India/US footprint is customer-serving capacity, not forward integration toward an end consumer.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Growth of 46% in FY26 and ~45% average over seven quarters, with three large US customers onboarded, new defence/aerospace/semiconductor wins and expansion into Southeast Asia and Europe, strongly implies share gain — and it is profitable share (ROCE 20.6%, NWC improving to 112 days, net debt/equity 0.06), not bought; but management never cites explicit market-share numbers or names competitors.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Our average revenue growth over the last 7 quarters has been 45%.

CULTURE.rationale: Guidance was raised three times inside FY26 (18-20% to 23-25% to 28-30% to ~40%) and then beaten at 46%; the working-capital promise of 120-130 days was beaten at 112; the FY24-FY27 doubling commitment was hit a year early; and management discloses the US manufacturing loss openly (~INR5 crores in Q4, narrowing, breakeven targeted late FY27) while keeping net debt/equity at 0.06.
CULTURE.quote: We delivered a 46% revenue growth for the full year, higher than our 40% guidance.

MOATTEST.rationale: There are real, articulable barriers — multi-quarter prototype-to-production qualification cycles, aerospace first article inspection, Kavach approval, semiconductor project readiness, and the dual US-India footprint that competitors cannot assemble quickly — plus deep box-build integration; but EMS remains a crowded industry where a well-funded entrant can build lines, and nothing here is time- or data-barrier proof in the jet-engine sense.
MOATTEST.quote: Box build has increased from 44% 4 years ago to 56% in Q4 FY26. This highlights the deep integration we have with our customers and drive stickiness
